To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) autistic individuals show a mismatch in their sensory abilities across individuals, (2) that this mismatch can lead to difficulties in social interactions and (3) that these difficulties are not only due to an inability to register social cues, but also due to a lack of integration of social cues and an inability to automatically and flexibly respond to them.

Autism is characterized by difficulties of integrating sensory information with social cues, which in turn lead to difficulties of anticipating social cues and responding to them in an appropriate and timely manner, which in turn can lead to social difficulties.

(1) social difficulties are not restricted to a mere deficit in social cue perception but are also related to differences in social cue integration and automatic responding, (2) the degree of such differences is related to the degree of autistic traits and (3) these differences may only manifest in sufficiently complex social contexts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the sensory, social, and motor domains are related and how they interact in autism.
a comprehensive approach to autism that considers both the sensory and social aspects of the disorder.
how individuals with and without autism process, learn from, and respond to social information in real-life social situations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
autism is characterized by an inability to integrate social information, which is crucially related to the individual’s action control and social behavior.
autism is a condition, where the integration of social and perceptual processes, which are essential to action control, is impaired.
the social difficulties of individuals with autism are due to a mismatch in their ability to perceive social cues, which in turn leads to difficulties in the automatic processing of social cues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
autistic individuals have a different, yet equally functional way of perceiving, learning from, and acting on the social environment.

the social difficulties in autism are not only a matter of sensory or social impairments, but that they are also related to a specific action control system, that is, a specific action perception-action coupling.
autism is characterized by a complex interplay between sensory and social deficits, which are reflected in the way people interact and respond to each other in social settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interrelationship between perceptuomotor and social processes is a promising approach to better understand the mechanisms underlying social difficulties in autism.
social difficulties in autism might not only stem from sensory or social impairments, but rather from a combination of both.
social difficulties are not only related to a general deficit in social cognition, but rather to an inability to integrate social information in an adaptive manner.
